report_name: UK NCSC: AI-Powered Ransomware to Hit Critical Infrastructure by 2028

threat_actors.name: Russia-affiliated threat actors
threat_actors.description: Nation-state actors backed by Russia, identified by the NCSC as the 'most audacious threat' expected to use AI to increase the speed and scale of attacks against UK critical infrastructure.
threat_actors.goals: To conduct cyber espionage and disruptive attacks against UK Critical National Infrastructure.

threat_actors.name: China-affiliated threat actors
threat_actors.description: Nation-state linked groups from China, identified by the NCSC as the most 'sustained cyber challenge facing the UK', expected to integrate AI into their cyber operations.
threat_actors.goals: To conduct cyber espionage and disruptive attacks against UK Critical National Infrastructure.

threat_actors.name: Financially motivated cybercriminals
threat_actors.description: Cybercriminal groups identified by the NCSC as key adopters of AI technology to enhance ransomware attacks for financial gain.
threat_actors.goals: To execute ransomware attacks against organizations for financial extortion.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The NCSC assesses that AI will be used to make ransomware attacks more sophisticated, including autonomously selecting high-value targets for encryption within critical infrastructure networks.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: The NCSC predicts that threat actors will use AI to enhance social engineering capabilities, such as creating more convincing phishing emails to gain initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Develop Capabilities
attack_patterns.description: The NCSC report states that AI will be used by threat actors as a force multiplier to enhance malware development capabilities.

attack_patterns.name: Active Scanning
attack_patterns.description: The NCSC report indicates that AI will enhance threat actors' capabilities in vulnerability discovery, suggesting automated and scaled-up scanning for weaknesses.

attack_patterns.name: Impair Defenses
attack_patterns.description: The NCSC warns that AI could be used in attacks to dynamically evade security controls, making ransomware more difficult to defend against.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
attack_patterns.description: The use of PowerShell with encoded commands was listed as a detectable pattern associated with threats to critical infrastructure.

attack_patterns.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
attack_patterns.description: The use of encoded PowerShell commands ('powershell.exe -enc') was highlighted as a specific command-line pattern to monitor for, indicating command obfuscation.

tools.name: Artificial Intelligence
tools.description: Identified by the NCSC as a 'force multiplier' for threat actors, enhancing their capabilities in vulnerability discovery, social engineering, and malware development to increase the speed and scale of attacks.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description: The use of encoded PowerShell commands was cited as a specific command-line pattern for defenders to monitor, indicating its use by threat actors in this context.

identities.name: National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC)
identities.description: The UK's national cybersecurity authority that authored the annual report warning of AI-powered ransomware threats.

identities.name: UK Critical National Infrastructure (CNI)
identities.description: The collective of UK critical infrastructure sectors identified by the NCSC as the primary target for future AI-powered ransomware attacks.

indicators.name: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
id: 2b9a8c7d-e1f3-4b6a-9c8d-0123456789ab
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of powershell.exe with the '-enc' flag, which indicates an encoded command. This is a common technique used by attackers to obfuscate malicious scripts.
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/ncsc-ai-ransomware-threat-uk-cni/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-04
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1027.010
  - attack.execution
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: ' -enc '
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of PowerShell with an encoded command, a technique highlighted in the article's cyber observables section.
